name: Employment Kirklees
organisation: Kirklees Council with delivery by C+K Careers and Paddock Trust
whoFor: Employment Kirklees works with residents who are unemployed, inactive, at risk of redundancy, working in high-risk sectors, under-employed residents working a low number of hours, residents on zero hours contracts; including graduates or anyone looking to progress or reskill
eligibility: Lives in Kirklees, whether employed or unemployed
Looking for support into work, apprenticeships, in-work progression or self-employment, or looking for new skills, learning or training
exclusions: We cannot support anyone who does not have the right to work in the UK
gate: Lives in Kirklees, whether employed or unemployed
Looking for support into work, apprenticeships, in-work progression or self-employment, or looking for new skills, learning or training
referralRoutes: Online enquiry and registration on My Kirklees ('Make an enquiry to Employment and Skills Support'): https://my.kirklees.gov.uk/service/Jobs_and_training___Make_an_enquiry_to_Employment_and_Skills_Support
In person - via Step by Step provision across Kirklees https://www.paddocktrust.org.uk/step-by-step
Partner referral, including Kirklees Council Employment & Skills Service, Welfare Provision, Kirklees Home and Neighbours, Kirklees In2Care

selfReferral.note: Referrals to Employment Kirklees can be by phone, website or referral partners

projects.name: One-to-one employment support
projects.overview: Starts with an assessment of the person's situation, skills and goals. Covers strengths and transferable skills, CVs, job applications and interviews, benefits and financial advice, and volunteering, training and education opportunities. Helps with barriers such as childcare, low confidence or lack of skills.
projects.duration: Flexible and open-ended, at the person's own pace

workExperience: Volunteering and work-related opportunities may be identified as part of the personalised action plan.
notes: Status before November 2026: Live - open to referrals
